reasoning_traces.think:
The core modeling framework employs a self-exciting point process extended with random memory, where event intensity dynamically switches between a 'hot' state (high intensity) and a 'regular' state (baseline intensity). The switching mechanism is governed by a hidden semi-Markov process S(t), which activates when the elapsed time since the last event is less than a latent memory duration τ. This formulation addresses the unrealistic infinite-memory assumption of classical Hawkes processes by introducing a finite excitation window. The conditional intensity function λ(t|H(t),τ,Z) is piecewise defined: λ_1(t|H(t),Z) when S(t)=1, and λ_0(t|H(t),Z) when S(t)=0. The model uses maximum likelihood estimation with Monte Carlo EM to infer τ and model parameters. Covariates Z (e.g., score difference, time of match) influence both the baseline intensity and the switching behavior. The resulting model allows for transient bursts of events, such as corner kicks, to be captured with realistic temporal decay. In GSI, this translates to probabilistic scoring burst modeling; in GSE, it enables dynamic in-game state transitions reflecting momentum shifts.
